[[File:Roger Charles Carolin DistV2.png|thumb|Collecting locations in Australia]]
'''Roger Charles Carolin''' (15 October 1929 – 3 February 2025) was an Australian botanist and [[pteridologist]].<ref name=anbg/> He was appointed a lecturer in botany at the [[University of Sydney]] in 1955,<ref name=anbg/>  earned a Ph.D. from there in 1962 with a thesis on the floral morphology of the campanales,<ref name=camp>Carolin, R.C. (1962) [https://trove.nla.gov.au/version/26557671 The floral morphology of the campanales sens.] Ph.D. thesis, University of Sydney. Retrieved 11 May 2019.</ref> and retired as an associate professor at the university in 1989.<ref name=anbg/>

Much of his research focused on the Campanulales, in particular the families Brunoniaceae and Goodeniaceae.<ref name=anbg/>  He co-authored the ''Flora of the Sydney Region'' (various editions: 1972–1993), and served on the editorial committees for the ''Flora of Central Australia'' and the ''Flora of Australia''. Carolin was the principal author of ''Flora of Australia'' Vol. 35. Brunoniaceae, Goodeniaceae (1992).<ref name=anbg/>

Carolin died on 3 February 2025, at the age of 95.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://funeralannouncement.com.au/roger-ruari-carolin|title=Roger (Ruari) Carolin|date=February 2025|access-date=22 February 2025|website=Funeral Announcements}}</ref>
